title: Computational Math: CS Degree
description: Liberty University's 2026-2027 BS in Computational Mathematics: Computer Science degree completion plan (120 credits) -- gen ed, Christianity core, and the full math/CS major sequence, mirrored from the official plan.

units.title: Communication & Information Literacy
units.gate: Confirm which electives in this block are already satisfied by transfer credit before enrolling -- Info Literacy Elective I is satisfied by CSIS 110, shared with Major Foundational Courses, so it isn't a separate course to take.

objectives.text: Communications elective -- choose 3 credits from COMS 101, BUSI 300, ENGR 270, or GICE 220
Information Literacy Elective I -- satisfied by CSIS 110 (shared credit from Major Foundational Courses)

Information Literacy Elective II -- choose 3 credits from ARTS 209, BUSI 201, CSIS 100, CSIS 110, CSIS 111, ENGL 102, ENGL 103, GEOG 200, HIEU 201, HIEU 202, HIUS 221, HIUS 222, HIUS 341, HIUS 360, HIUS 380, HIWD 370, or WRSP 101

units.title: Technological Solutions & Quantitative Reasoning
units.gate: The Math Elective here is satisfied by MATH 131, shared with Major Foundational Courses -- don't schedule it as a second course.

objectives.text: Math elective -- satisfied by MATH 131 (shared credit from Major Foundational Courses)

units.title: Critical Thinking
units.gate: Pick a Critical Thinking elective that won't double up with a course you're already taking elsewhere in gen ed -- several PHIL/ENGL options here overlap in skillset with the Civic & Global Engagement block.

objectives.text: Critical Thinking elective -- choose 3 credits from ARTS 105, ARTS 205, ARTS 214, BUSI 205, ENGL 201, ENGL 202, ENGL 216, ENGL 221, ETHC 101, ETHC 205, PHIL 201, or PHIL 240

units.title: Civic & Global Engagement
units.gate: Choose the Cultural Studies elective based on what you can actually transfer in, if applicable -- the approved list spans languages, government, and religion, so options vary widely in workload.

objectives.text: Cultural Studies elective -- choose 3 credits from ARTS 105, CSTU 101, CSTU 220, GICE 290, GOVT 200, GOVT 220, MUSC 103, or RLGN 210

units.title: Social & Scientific Inquiry
units.gate: Pick a Natural Science elective with a lab component in mind if you'll need one later -- not all options in the approved list include one.

objectives.text: Natural Science elective -- choose 3 credits from BIOL 101, BIOL 102, ETHC 210, NASC 210, PHSC 121, PHSC 122, PHSC 210, PHYS 101, PHYS 201, or PHYS 231
Social Science elective -- choose 3 credits from BUSI 223, BUSI 240, ECON 110, ECON 213, ECON 214, HLTH 252, PSYC 101, PSYC 210, SOCI 200, or SOCI 201

units.title: Christianity & Contexts
units.gate: Check transfer-credit waivers before scheduling these -- students transferring in 45+ UG credits have RLGN 104 waived, and 60+ UG credits also waives THEO 104.

objectives.text: Survey of Old and New Testament (BIBL 104)

units.title: CSIS 110: Introduction to Computer Science
units.gate: Earn a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major foundational course, and this is a prerequisite the entire CS cognate sequence is built on.

objectives.text: Programming languages and how compilers translate code
Operating systems and how applications run on them
Computing ethics: intellectual property, privacy, and computer crime

units.title: MATH 131: Calculus and Analytic Geometry I
units.gate: Earn a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major foundational course, and this is a prerequisite the entire math core sequence is built on.

objectives.text: Functions and graphs, including exponential, logarithmic, and inverse trig forms
The derivative: formal definition and differentiation rules
Applications of derivatives, including L'Hopital's Rule

units.title: MATH 132: Calculus and Analytic Geometry II
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course, and this feeds directly into Discrete Mathematics and Multivariable Calculus.

objectives.text: Applications of integration: area, volume, and arc length
Sequences, infinite series, and convergence tests

units.title: MATH 211: Introduction to Statistical Analysis
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course.

objectives.text: Probability theory foundations for calculus-trained students
Statistical inference: estimation and hypothesis testing
Regression and correlation between data sets

units.title: MATH 250: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course, and this is a prerequisite for Linear Algebra, Multivariable Calculus, and CSIS 215.

units.title: MATH 345: Introduction to the History of Mathematics
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course. This one has a heavy upper-level-math prerequisite list, so schedule it after several 300/400-level math courses, not early.

objectives.text: Ancient mathematics: Egyptian, Babylonian, and early number systems
Greek geometry: Euclid, Pythagoras, and Archimedes
The development of algebra and algebraic notation
The invention of calculus: Newton and Leibniz
Foundations of set theory and modern mathematics

units.title: MATH 410: Matrix and Linear Algebra
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course, and this is load-bearing: it underpins Numerical Methods and Abstract Algebraic Structures.

objectives.text: Systems of linear equations and Gaussian elimination

units.title: MATH 412: Numerical Methods
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course. Requires Matrix and Linear Algebra as a prerequisite.

units.title: MATH 423: Abstract Algebraic Structures
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course. Requires Matrix and Linear Algebra as a prerequisite.

units.title: MATH 430: Multivariable Calculus
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course, and this is load-bearing: it's a prerequisite for both Applied Differential Equations and Mathematical Modeling and Simulation.

objectives.text: Limits, continuity, and differentiation for functions of several variables
Integration and power series in several variables
Analytic geometry of curves and surfaces
Vector fields and integration along curves and surfaces
The major theorems of vector calculus: Green's, Stokes', and the Divergence Theorem

units.title: MATH 432: Applied Differential Equations
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course, and this is a prerequisite for Mathematical Modeling and Simulation and the Capstone.

objectives.text: Applications: population growth, mechanical vibrations, and circuits

units.title: MATH 441: Probability I
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course.

objectives.text: Set notation and operations applied to probability
Expected value and discrete probability distributions

units.title: MATH 460: Mathematical Modeling and Simulation
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course. Requires Applied Differential Equations as a prerequisite.

objectives.text: Formulating mathematical models from real-world scenarios
Analytical techniques for evaluating model behavior

units.title: STAT 420: Regression and Forecasting I
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course. Calculus-based, not just applied stats -- it leans on Calculus I and Intro to Statistical Analysis.

objectives.text: Model diagnostics and checking regression assumptions
Applying regression to a real dataset

units.title: MATH 491: Computational Mathematics Capstone
units.gate: Senior standing required -- this is the last math course in the sequence, sitting after Applied Differential Equations.

objectives.text: Independent capstone project synthesizing the computational math major
Applying computational techniques to a substantial problem
Written and oral presentation of results

units.title: CSIS 100: Introduction to Information Sciences and Systems
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course.

objectives.text: Evaluating and choosing business technology solutions
Mapping business processes to where technology adds value
Aligning IT strategy with organizational goals
Technical writing for information systems documentation

units.title: CSIS 111: Introduction to Programming Using C++
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course, and CSIS 112 and CSIS 215 both assume the fluency this course is supposed to build, not just a passing grade in it.

units.title: CSIS 112: Advanced Programming Using C++
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course, and this is a prerequisite for Algorithms and Data Structures.

objectives.text: Introductory data structures: arrays and lists

units.title: CSIS 215: Algorithms and Data Structures
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course. Requires both Advanced Programming Using C++ and Introduction to Discrete Mathematics as prerequisites.

objectives.text: Sorting, searching, and table access algorithms
Implementing abstract data types with C++ classes

units.title: CSIS 340: Studies in Information Security
units.gate: Maintain a C or higher -- Liberty requires it for every major course.

objectives.text: Fundamental principles of information system security
Common attacker tactics and how controls get bypassed

units.title: Free Electives
units.gate: No courses are specified -- use these credits deliberately (e.g. a minor, a second language, or extra CS depth) rather than defaulting to whatever fills a schedule gap.

objectives.text: 22 credits of free electives, any 100-400 level course not already required elsewhere in the plan

units.title: Graduation Requirements
units.gate: Track these five gates independently of credit totals -- it's possible to have enough overall credits and still miss the upper-level or Liberty-residency minimums.

objectives.text: Minimum 120 credits overall applied to the program of study
Minimum 30 upper-level (300-400) credits applied to the program
Minimum 13.75 Liberty credits applied to the major
Minimum 30 Liberty credits applied to the overall program of study
Submit the Degree Completion Application within the final semester before graduation

provenance.note: Objectives paraphrased from the publicly published exam guide or degree plan by the Ascendra project; unofficial; not affiliated with or endorsed by any vendor or credentialing body.
